chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yasin al-Darir, from Hariz, from one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him from where it is appropriate to take the pebbles of Jamaraat? He said: 'Do not take them from two places: from outside the Haram and from the pebbles of Jamaraat themselves, and there is no harm in taking them from the rest of the Haram.'
And whenever he takes the pebbles from outside the Haram, that does not suffice; it was narrated.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Where should one collect the pebbles for Rami al-Jamarat during Hajj according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the geographical boundaries for collecting pebbles for Rami al-Jamarat, emphasizing that validity depends on the location being within the Haram but distinct from the existing Jamaraat pile. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the sanctity of the specific ritual site, ensuring the pebbles used are not merely recycled from the previous year's stones but are freshly gathered from the sacred precincts. The distinction between 'outside the Haram' and 'the Jamaraat pile itself' highlights the precision required in Hajj rituals to maintain their symbolic integrity.
